title: Smoothing Exponents and Decoupling in Semifinite von Neumann Algebras
authors: Zhiwen Lin, Hongsen Qiu, Xinyu Zhang
abstract: We study the smoothing exponent of the max-relative entropy in semifinite von Neumann algebras. Our main result gives an exact exponent formula in this setting. The proof develops operator-algebraic replacements for the dimension-dependent tools used in finite-dimensional arguments. These ingredients show that the smoothing exponent is governed by the underlying von Neumann algebraic structure rather than by matrix dimension estimates. As an application, we formulate catalytic quantum information decoupling with a semifinite von Neumann algebraic reference system. We prove an intrinsic layer-cake lemma for von Neumann algebras, which removes the countable spectrum assumption in the finite-dimensional proof and yields the corresponding semifinite estimate. Consequently, the decoupling reliability exponent is described by the same sandwiched Rényi mutual information formula as in the finite-dimensional theory.
summary: This theoretical paper extends concepts from finite-dimensional quantum information theory—specifically smoothing exponents and decoupling bounds—to the general setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras. By developing new operator-algebraic tools, the authors establish exact formulas showing that these fundamental physical limits depend only on the underlying algebraic structure, not on artificial dimension truncations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the smoothing exponent of the max-relative entropy and develops a framework for catalytic quantum information decoupling within the mathematical setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras.
main_result: They derive exact exponent formulas showing that these quantities are governed by the underlying algebraic structure rather than finite matrix dimension estimates, generalizing known results to infinite dimensions.
method: The methodology involves developing operator-algebraic replacements for finite-dimensional tools and utilizing noncommutative L^p-spaces associated with semifinite von Neumann algebras.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework is built upon general quantum systems described by semifinite von Neumann algebras (VNA), extending beyond simple matrix models. Concepts from quantum information theory, such as Rényi relative entropies and divergences, are central to the analysis.
key_observables: Smoothing exponent, max-relative entropy ($D_\infty$), decoupling reliability exponent, and sandwiched Rényi mutual information.
important_parameters: The parameter $s$ (related to the order of the divergence) is crucial for optimization; limits as dimension/index go to infinity are key.
main_assumptions: The primary technical challenge overcome is moving from finite-dimensional arguments to the general semifinite setting, requiring intrinsic algebraic tools.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing foundational $L^p$-space definitions on VNA, defining generalized information divergences, proving key continuity lemmas (like for Legendre transforms), and finally applying these results to derive the exponent formulas for decoupling and smoothing.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to analyze quantum resource theories (like entanglement or coherence) in infinite-dimensional settings relevant to continuous variable systems or large quantum memories, which is highly relevant for advanced quantum information theory.
